questions.prompt: Why is a CVSS base score not the same as your risk?

options.text: CVSS measures intrinsic severity; risk also depends on exposure, asset value, and active exploitation
CVSS already includes your specific environment perfectly
Risk is always exactly the CVSS score
CVSS only applies to physical security

questions.explanation: CVSS scores intrinsic severity; a Critical on an unreachable system may pose less risk than a Medium on your internet-facing crown jewel.

questions.prompt: Match each reference to what it is.

pairs.right: Catalog of vulnerabilities exploited in the wild

questions.explanation: A CVE names a flaw, CVSS scores its severity, CWE names the weakness type, and the CISA KEV catalog lists vulnerabilities known to be exploited.
The continuous loop runs inventory → scan → prioritize → remediate → verify — you can't secure what you don't know you have.

questions.prompt: Which signals should inform how you prioritize a vulnerability? Select all that apply.

options.text: Whether it is actively exploited (CISA KEV / EPSS)
The asset's exposure and business value
The alphabetical order of the CVE ID

questions.explanation: Prioritize with severity plus real exploitation and exposure/asset value; the CVE's alphabetical order is irrelevant.

questions.prompt: The CISA ____ catalog lists vulnerabilities known to be exploited in the wild and should be fixed first.
questions.explanation: The CISA Known Exploited Vulnerabilities (KEV) catalog flags flaws confirmed exploited, the strongest urgency signal for patching.

questions.prompt: How does vulnerability scanning differ from penetration testing?

options.text: Scanning is automated breadth; a pen test is skilled manual depth that chains flaws to prove impact
Scanning finds more exploitable chains than a pen test
A pen test never requires authorization

questions.explanation: Scanning gives automated breadth across many known issues; penetration testing adds manual depth, chaining weaknesses to demonstrate real, exploitable impact.
